name: Elihu
overview: Elihu was a male chief officer among the Judahites, serving in a significant leadership role within the tribe of Judah. He is uniquely identified as a brother of David, highlighting his close familial connection to one of Israel's most important biblical figures. This relationship situates Elihu within the royal and tribal leadership context of ancient Israel.
namesAndTitles: The name Elihu means 'y-h-v-h is [my] G-d,' reflecting a theistic declaration common in Hebrew names. This proper name emphasizes a personal relationship with the LORD, though it was not given by God directly. Elihu's name thus reveals a faith-centered identity consistent with the biblical worldview.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Elihu was a brother of David, establishing a direct familial link to the Israelite king. Beyond this, no other family relationships are documented for Elihu in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Elihu's significance lies in his role as a chief officer for the Judahites and his close kinship with David, which implies involvement in the governance and administration during David's time. His mention in 1 Chronicles 27:18 places him within the organized leadership structure of Israel, underscoring the importance of faithful and capable leaders in God's providential plan for His people. Elihu exemplifies the godly leadership that supported David's reign and the establishment of Israel as a nation under God.
